You can attach the zip file and instructions in either of the following ways:

1. **Drag and Drop**: Drag the `.zip` file directly from your computer into the chat box or onto the conversation window.
2. **Attachment / Plus Icon**: Click the attachment icon (the paperclip or **`+`** icon) next to the message input box at the bottom of the chat to browse and select your file.
3. **Instructions**: 
   - You can paste the instructions directly into the message box alongside your uploaded file, or
   - Include them as a text/markdown file (e.g., `README.md` or `instructions.txt`) inside or alongside the zip.

Once you upload the zip file and share your instructions, I will inspect and extract the contents, review your current web stack and architecture, and start porting it to a mobile app according to your requirements.

I see the assignment requirements from your image:
1. **APK download link** (uploaded to Google Drive or similar).
2. **Repository link** (GitHub repository containing the mobile app source code).
3. **Video demonstration** (demonstrating the mobile app interacting/matching your eCommerce website).

---

### How to share your web application files

The chat file uploader often restricts `.zip` archives or large files. Here are the easiest ways to share your web app:

1. **Google Drive / Cloud Link (Recommended)**:
   - Upload your `.zip` file to Google Drive (or Dropbox / OneDrive / WeTransfer).
   - Set the link access to **"Anyone with the link can view"** and paste the link here. I can download and unpack it directly into our workspace.
2. **Share a Live Website / Hosted URL**:
   - If your Lesson 2 eCommerce site is already hosted online (Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, etc.), you can share the link.
3. **Paste Code Directly**:
   - If it is a relatively lightweight project (e.g., HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or a few key React components/API routes), you can paste the key code files directly into the chat.
4. **Rename the File Extension**:
   - If the file picker is only filtering out `.zip` extensions, try renaming your file to `project.zip.txt` or `project.zip.png` and uploading it.

---

> [!TIP]
> **For the GitHub Repository Requirement:** 
> When you're ready to submit your GitHub repository link, you can tap the **GitHub icon at the top of the chat** to connect a repository. Your entire project history and mobile app source code will sync there automatically.

Whenever you're able to share the link or files, let me know and we'll get started building your mobile app!
